findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an AC (and corresponding unit test) that positively asserts `run()` still mutates `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` when temperature is withdrawn — e.g., call the runner twice with a supports_temperature=False cap and assert the log/warning fires only once (dedup preserved).
evidence: AC reads: 'the `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` mutation still happens in run(), and test_structured_run_has_no_runtime_import_from_runner passes' — the test cited only verifies ABSENCE from the leaf, not PRESENCE in run()
The leaf-import AST walk fires if the mutation moves INTO structured_run.py, but goes green if the mutation is simply deleted from run() entirely
Changed/deleted behavior (dedup log call site) gets no positive behavioral test work
findings.finding: The plan requires the `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED` dedup-log mutation to stay in `run()` after the extraction, but no AC (or existing test) positively asserts that `run()` still performs this mutation — only that `build_model_settings` does NOT (via the leaf-import test). An implementer who deletes the mutation entirely satisfies every stated AC while silently dropping the dedup-logging behavior.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — `build_model_settings performs no side effect` bullet; 'THE LEAF-INVARIANT TRAP' section
scenarios: Implementer deletes `_TEMPERATURE_WITHDRAWN_LOGGED.add(resolved)` from run() rather than leaving it there; all ACs pass; dedup-logging silently stops working, repeated temperature-withdrawal warnings flood logs in production
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: 'a test drives run() (or the temperature block directly) with a supports_temperature=False caps record twice and asserts the withdrawal log fires exactly once (dedup guard preserved in run()). This complements the leaf-import test which only proves the mutation is absent from structured_run.py, not present in run().'

findings.finding: The plan has an extended section mandating that `cache_settings` MUST BE A PARAMETER (not recomputed inside `build_model_settings`), explaining a concrete silent-bug failure mode if violated, but no acceptance criterion verifies this constraint. An implementer who recomputes `cache_settings_for(caps)` inside the extracted function would pass every AC (temperature tests, LOC tests, import/removal tests, seam guard tests) while silently re-enabling cache settings on the TestModel path.
findings.location: AC list (all items) vs. `cache_settings MUST BE A PARAMETER` subsection
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the AC list: '- [ ] a test asserts that `build_model_settings(..., cache_settings=None, ...)` returns a dict with no cache-related keys regardless of `caps`, and that `build_model_settings(..., cache_settings={"k": "v"}, ...)` includes those keys — confirming the value flows from the parameter, not from a re-invocation of `cache_settings_for(caps)` inside the function.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a proving command for the second-module 100-LOC floor on the conditional split path, e.g. `wc -l <second_module>.py | awk '$1 >= 100'`, or extend the seam test to cover any new extraction module.
evidence: 'If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module at or above the 100-LOC floor'
No corresponding seam test assertion is mentioned for a second module
findings.finding: If a split to a second module is required, the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor for THAT second module has no machine enforcement — the seam test (`100 <= loc < 500`) only covers `structured_run.py`.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria — 'the extracted module is at or above the 100-LOC anti-fragmentation floor'
scenarios: An implementer creates a thin second module (e.g. 60 LOC) containing only one function to avoid the ceiling; the AC text says 'at or above 100 LOC' but no test enforces it for the new file, so CI stays green while the anti-fragmentation invariant is violated.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
verify command `wc -l src/rebar/llm/runner.py` inspects output with `wc` but asserts nothing — add an exit-code or comparison (-q, [ "$(...)" -eq N ], jq -e) so a failure is observable
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State a default candidate name for the fallback split module (e.g. `src/rebar/llm/model_settings.py`) so the executor does not have to invent one if the 500-LOC ceiling is breached.
evidence: 'If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module at or above the 100-LOC floor'
No candidate module name is given for the split path
findings.finding: If the conditional split path is taken (both functions plus comments would breach structured_run.py's 500-LOC ceiling), the plan does not name the second themed module, leaving an executor to choose arbitrarily.
findings.location: ## Destination and its headroom (do not create a new file) — paragraph ending 'split along a real seam into a second themed module'
scenarios: An implementer who finds the combined extraction would push structured_run.py past 500 LOC must invent a module name, potentially producing an inconsistently themed file or a name conflict with a future plan.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence: 'If a split is required, place the settings functions in `src/rebar/llm/model_settings.py`.' This gives an executor a concrete name without constraining the primary path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the contradiction between the absolute 'do not create a new file' heading and the conditional 'split into a second themed module' body instruction — either drop the contingent split (since 373 + ~80 = ~453 < 500 by measurement) or rewrite the heading to 'prefer the existing module; split only if 500 LOC is breached'.
evidence: Section heading: 'Destination and its headroom (do not create a new file)'
Body text: 'If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module at or above the 100-LOC floor — do NOT trim the comments to fit'
These two directives are mutually exclusive when LOC is close to 500.
findings.finding: The section heading 'Destination and its headroom (do not create a new file)' states an absolute constraint, but the body of that same section conditionally permits creating a new file: 'If both functions plus their travelling comments would breach 500, split along a real seam into a second themed module.' An implementer near the 500-LOC boundary would face two directly contradictory instructions from the same section.
findings.location: Section: 'Destination and its headroom (do not create a new file)'
scenarios: An implementer whose extracted content lands between 480–500 LOC has no guidance on which instruction takes precedence.
If the extraction plus comments does breach 500, the implementer cannot simultaneously 'not create a new file' and 'split into a second themed module'.
findings.suggested_fix: Since the plan's own measurement shows ~453 LOC after extraction (well under 500), drop the contingent split instruction and keep the heading's absolute constraint, or rewrite as: 'Destination: structured_run.py. Do not create a new file unless extraction would breach 500 LOC, in which case split at a real seam above the 100-LOC floor.'
